newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils close higher, palm trade active.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils close higher, palm trade active.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices closed mostly higher on Wednesday following early gains on the Chicago futures markets.
Trading in crude palm oil was fairly active during the afternoon with consumers and shippers involved.
Earlier prices had firmed following gains in Asia where Malaysian palm oil prices were supported by higher-than-expected export figures for the first 10 days of November.
Malaysian cargo surveyor Caleb Brett estimated local palm oil exports during the first 10 days of November at 207,000 tonnes.
Although this was lower than in the same period during October it was above expectations of the local market.
In Europe crude palm oil cif closed unchanged to $7.50 up after Nov traded at $550 and $560, Dec at $545 and $550, Jan/Mar at $540 and Apr/Jun at $537.50 a tonne cif.
Among refined oil RBD palm oil finished $10 to $7.50 up and olein $5 to $10 up with no further business reported during the afternoon.
Coconut oil finished unchanged to $10 up after Nov/Dec traded at $770.
Nov/Dec was reported to have traded early in the day in a switch with Dec/Jan with a $25 difference.
Dutch soy oil closed with gains of around 1.50 guilders after Dec traded at 86, Jan at 87 and Aug/Oct at 92.50 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Dutch/EU rape oil was 0.50 to one guilders up after Dec fetched 92 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Based on sellers' prices the premium for rape oil over soy oil was 4.50 to five guilders at the close against five to 5.50 guilders on Tuesday.
